# CEO Plan: User Dashboard Page
Generated by /plan-ceo-review (via /autoplan) on 2026-09-10
Branch: main | Mode: SELECTIVE EXPANSION
Repo: gstack-autoplan-chain-bwDe8x (no remote)
Source plan: `.claude/plans/ui-heavy-feature.md` (this document records scope decisions; the full reviewed plan with obligations lives in the active plan file)

## Baseline plan (what the source plan asks for)

A new page at `/dashboard` that members land on after login, behind the existing member-cohort feature flag. Three panels: `QuickActions` (the existing action registry's three actions: create an item, resume assigned work, invite a member, each with a stable ID, label, route target, and server-side eligibility predicate), `NotificationsPanel` (member-specific alerts with persistent read state, from the existing member-scoped list method, latest 20), `ActivityFeed` (immutable workspace audit history, from the existing workspace-scoped list method, latest 20). One new endpoint `GET /api/dashboard` composes those three existing repository calls. A "Mark all as read" confirmation modal calls the existing idempotent member-scoped bulk-read API, which marks only notifications at or before a supplied snapshot time. A toast system gives nonblocking feedback. The "current landing" page is whatever members see after login today; the flag's rollback target.

## Constraints (from the source plan)

- No schema migration. No new mutation API. The only write reuses the existing bulk-read API.
- Member and workspace IDs come from the request context (cookie session plus workspace membership middleware); never from query parameters. Mutations require CSRF tokens.
- Dark mode and personalization are separate plans; action ranking does not exist and is not built here.
- Existing primitives to reuse: Tailwind tokens, responsive page shell, buttons, links, dialog primitive (focus trap, Escape, focus return), typed HTTP errors (unauthenticated, forbidden, validation, retryable-service, network), Vitest, React Testing Library, Playwright, fixtures (authenticated member, another workspace, empty lists, service failures), feature flags, request and error metrics.
- Accessibility policy: named controls, live region for nonblocking feedback, sufficient contrast, reduced-motion support.
- Blast radius for auto-approved expansions: the dashboard page, its panels, the new endpoint, and their direct importers. The login flow and global key handling are outside it.

## Success metric

- Metric: login-to-first-completed-task time. Events already recorded: `login`, `action start`, `action completion`, `permission error`. Definition: for each login, the elapsed time to the first `action completion` event by that member within 24 hours after login, regardless of session boundaries (logins with no completion in the window count as non-completions in the completed-task-rate guardrail, not as infinite durations in the median).
- Baseline: 75 s median from a team task walkthrough. This is not member data. Before the 10% rollout stage, the real distribution is pulled from the existing events and the target is restated relative to it.
- Target: 45 s median (from the source plan), restated as a relative improvement once the real baseline is measured.
- Guardrails: completed-task rate and permission-error rate must not be worse in the cohort than in control.
- Secondary: `dashboard_return_visit` rate (a page redirected-to but never returned-to is not a home).

## Vision

### 10x Check
The dashboard as a start-of-day surface that talks back. A member logs in and the page already knows their one assigned item and shows it as the single primary button. The moment a teammate mentions them, the alert appears without a refresh. Concrete shape: server-side next-action ranking, an SSE channel for live updates, keyboard-first quick actions. Effort for that vision: human ~3 weeks / CC ~5 h. Not this plan: ranking and personalization are the user's separate plans and SSE is new infrastructure. This plan builds the surface those features attach to.

### Effort for the accepted scope of this plan
Baseline plan plus all accepted items, hardening, instrumentation, rollout, and tests: human ~6 to 7 days / CC ~2 to 2.5 hours.

## Scope Decisions

| # | Proposal | Effort | Decision | Reasoning |
|---|----------|--------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Unread count in the document title | S | ACCEPTED | In blast radius (page component); a background tab tells the member something changed |
| 2 | Snapshot-rule copy in the mark-all-read modal | XS | ACCEPTED | Makes the existing API's snapshot semantics visible; depends on assumption A2 below, with a fallback |
| 3 | Relative timestamps with absolute time in `title` and `<time datetime>` | S | ACCEPTED | One small util used by two panels; screen-reader and hover clarity |
| 4 | Skeletons sized to the final layout (no layout shift) | S | ACCEPTED | Part of the loading state the plan already requires |
| 5 | Per-panel retry with backoff and "Last updated" stamp | S | ACCEPTED | Part of the error/retry state the plan already requires |
| 6 | Deep links from every activity and notification row | S | ACCEPTED | The row is the shortest path to the next task; directly serves the metric |
| 7 | Teaching empty states pointing at quick actions | XS | ACCEPTED | Empty states are features; costs copy only |
| 8 | Shared `PanelFrame` component | S | ACCEPTED | Three panels with four states each on day one; DRY with three consumers now, not a speculative abstraction |
| 9 | Shared toast primitive at app root with README | S | ACCEPTED | No toast exists anywhere in the app and the accessibility policy requires a live region for nonblocking feedback. A live region must be mounted at the app root to announce reliably, so the placement is a technical requirement, not generalization for its own sake. Differs from the rejected panel registry (#16), which would abstract over one consumer with no technical forcing function. |
| 10 | Prefetch dashboard payload on login submit | M | DEFERRED | Touches the login flow, outside this plan's blast radius |
| 11 | Keyboard shortcuts for quick actions | M | DEFERRED | Global key handling with conflict risk; not needed to hit the metric |
| 12 | SSE live updates | L | DEFERRED | New infrastructure; wait for return-visit data |
| 13 | Panel admission criterion | S | DEFERRED | A written team rule plus a process step (any new panel ships behind the same flag and must not worsen the metric). It is process, not code in this plan; recorded in TODOS.md so it exists before a second team adds a panel |
| 14 | Command palette | M | SKIPPED | Duplicates quick actions |
| 15 | Next-action ranking | L | SKIPPED | User's personalization plan; ranking does not exist |
| 16 | Server-driven panel registry | L | SKIPPED | Abstraction with one consumer and no forcing function; duplicates the personalization plan |
| 17 | Undo for mark-all-read instead of a modal | M | SKIPPED | Needs a new un-read mutation API; the constraints forbid new mutation APIs |

Items 1 to 9 are conditional on taste decision T2 resolving to dashboard-first (the recommended option). If the user chooses the redirect experiment instead, items 1 to 9 still apply to the dashboard when it ships, but the dashboard ships after the experiment reads out.

## Accepted Scope (added to this plan)

Terms used below: **pessimistic pending state** means the UI shows a disabled button and spinner until the server confirms, then applies the change (no optimistic update, no rollback code). **Monotonic sequence guard** means each dashboard request carries an incrementing number and any response whose number is lower than the latest issued request is discarded. **Refetch on mount only** means the whole-dashboard request runs when the page mounts and when the member presses a retry control; there is no timer-based polling. Per-panel retry (item 5) is a manual control that re-issues the whole dashboard request and re-renders only the panel that was in error from the new response. **Queue of 3** means at most three toasts are visible; a fourth waits and appears when one dismisses; nothing is dropped except under overflow: when all three visible toasts are persistent and a new toast arrives, the oldest persistent toast is dismissed to admit it. **Persistent errors** means error toasts have no auto-dismiss timer and stay until the member dismisses them. Identical toasts (same error code and same message text) coalesce.

Accepted Scope as written assumes taste decision T1 resolves to the aggregate endpoint (the recommended option). If T1 resolves to per-panel fetches, the hook, retry, `generatedAt`, and envelope items below are rewritten before implementation.

- Aggregate endpoint hardened: three repository calls in parallel; per-call timeout 2 s; whole-request timeout 3 s; server p95 budget 300 ms at 20 rows per panel (these three numbers are recommended defaults to confirm at the gate; the endpoint performance check on staging confirms upstream latencies fit inside them before the 10% stage); per-panel `{ status: "ok", data } | { status: "error", code }` envelope; server `generatedAt`; page-level all-fail state.
- Shared `PanelFrame` (loading with layout parity, teaching empty, error with retry and "Last updated" stamp, success).
- Shared toast primitive (live region `role="status"` `aria-live="polite"`, queue of 3, success auto-dismiss 6 s unless focused or hovered, persistent errors, reduced motion, short request reference on error toasts, README).
- Client hook: response shape validation, refetch on mount only, abort on unmount and on mark-all-read confirm, monotonic sequence guard.
- Mark-all-read: confirmation dialog on the existing primitive; snapshot-rule copy; pessimistic pending state; `generatedAt` as snapshot time; the "Mark all as read" control is rendered only when the notifications panel is in the success state with at least one unread item (never in loading, empty, or error state, so `generatedAt` is always from the same response as the items shown).
- Error to toast mapping for mark-all-read: CSRF validation failure or unauthenticated → persistent toast "Your session expired. Refresh the page and try again." with no state change; forbidden → persistent toast "You don't have access to do that."; retryable-service or network → persistent toast "Couldn't mark notifications as read." with a Retry action; success → "Marked N notifications as read." auto-dismiss.
- Text-only rendering of user-generated fields, deep links on rows, relative plus absolute time, title unread badge.
- Reading order quick actions → notifications → activity on every breakpoint; the "resume assigned work" action from the action registry is the primary-emphasis button; no greeting banner; panels are not three equal cards.
- Flag behavior: the existing member-cohort flag gates the `/dashboard` route and the post-login redirect target; an off-cohort member who visits `/dashboard` directly is redirected to the current landing page; a flag flip while a member is already on `/dashboard` takes effect on their next navigation or login (the current page is not torn down).
- Instrumentation: structured request log line; metrics `dashboard_request_duration_ms`, `dashboard_panel_result{panel,status}`, `dashboard_mark_all_read{result}`; analytics events `dashboard_exposed`, `dashboard_panel_rendered{panel,state}`, `dashboard_action_clicked{actionId}`, `dashboard_row_clicked{panel}`, `dashboard_view_all_clicked{panel}`, `dashboard_return_visit`. Logs and events ship with the dark deploy. Alert rules (panel error rate above 2% over 5 min, p95 above budget for 10 min, mark-all-read failure rate above 1%) and the day-1 funnel dashboard are configured before the internal-members stage so the first cohort is observed; they cost configuration only and reuse the existing metrics stack.
- Rollout stages and exit criteria: dark deploy (flag off; smoke test passes) → internal members (minimum 2 business days; zero alerts; funnel events arriving) → 10% (minimum 3 days; alerts quiet 24 h; guardrails flat; measured baseline recorded before entering) → 50% (minimum 2 weeks; kill criterion evaluated at the end) → 100%. Cohort selection uses the existing flag's member-cohort mechanism (stable per-member assignment). The feature owner advances a stage; any fired alert pauses advancement.
- Kill criterion (defaults to confirm at the gate): at the end of the 50% stage, if the cohort's median login-to-first-completed-task is not at least 20% better than control, or completed-task rate or permission-error rate is worse than control, the flag is turned off and only the component that moved the metric is kept.
- Full test matrix: unit (error mapping, `PanelFrame` states, hook sequencing and abort, toast queue, relative time with injected clock), integration (compose on fixtures: all-ok, one-fail, all-fail, one-timeout, unauthenticated, another-workspace isolation), Playwright (login → dashboard → quick action, mark-all-read flow, keyboard-only path through the dialog, axe scan, empty fixture, service-failure fixture, flag-off landing), endpoint p95 check on staging.
- Existing-code assumptions verified during implementation, each with a fallback:
  - A1: the activity list method preloads actor display names (no N+1). Verify by reading the method and its query. Fallback: add the preload to the existing method (small change to existing code, flagged as its own task).
  - A2: the bulk-read API accepts a caller-supplied snapshot time and validates or clamps it (rejecting future times). Verify by reading the API handler. Fallback if it rejects caller-supplied times: send no snapshot and let the API use server-now at submit; keep the modal copy but phrase it as "received before now". Fallback if it accepts unvalidated future times: flag as an existing-API finding; the dashboard still sends `generatedAt`, which is always in the past.
  - A3: the new route inherits the existing rate limits. Verify by reading the middleware chain. Fallback: register the route in the rate-limit configuration.

## Clarifications from spec review round 2

- Composition: two list calls (activity by workspace, notifications by member) plus the action registry's existing server-side eligibility evaluation, an in-process call. Only eligible actions are returned; ineligible actions are hidden, not disabled. Primary emphasis: "resume assigned work" when eligible, else "create an item", else "invite a member". Zero eligible actions shows the panel empty state and logs at warn.
- Per-panel retry is manual. "Backoff" means a cooldown on the retry button: disabled 2 s after a press, doubling to a maximum of 8 s on repeated failures. No automatic timed retry anywhere.
- Toast queue: identical persistent error toasts coalesce into one; if all three visible toasts are persistent and a new toast arrives, the oldest persistent toast is dismissed to make room, so success toasts always surface. Error toasts carry the response's request id header when present and omit it for network errors with no response.
- After a successful mark-all-read the panel locally marks items with `createdAt <= generatedAt` read and updates the title badge; no refetch required.
- Unread badge: use a total unread count field if the list response exposes one (assumption A5); otherwise show the count of unread items among the 20 fetched and display "20+" when all 20 are unread. Success toast: if the bulk-read API returns an affected count (assumption A4), "Marked N notifications as read."; otherwise "Marked your notifications as read."
- Unauthenticated on `GET /api/dashboard` redirects to login with `/dashboard` as the return path.
- Metric window: elapsed time from `login` to the member's first `action completion` within 24 h, regardless of session boundaries. Logins with no completion count against the completed-task-rate guardrail and are excluded from the median. `dashboard_return_visit` is a `/dashboard` view not preceded by a `login` event within 60 s on the same day. A new event `dashboard_row_clicked{panel}` records deep-link follows.
- Kill-criterion attribution: the panel whose `dashboard_action_clicked` or `dashboard_row_clicked` event immediately precedes the first `action completion` is credited; on flag-off, panels with credited completions are candidates to keep. The 20% kill floor is deliberately below the 40% improvement the 75 s → 45 s target implies.

## Deferred to TODOS.md
- Prefetch dashboard on login submit (P2, M → CC S). Depends on the dashboard shipping.
- Keyboard shortcuts for quick actions (P3, M → CC S). Announce shortcuts in button labels.
- SSE live updates for notifications and activity (P3, L → CC M). Depends on return-visit demand.
- Panel admission criterion: written team rule plus process step; any new panel ships behind the same flag and must not worsen login-to-first-completed-task (P2, S).

## Taste decisions carried to the Final Approval Gate
- T1: one aggregate endpoint with per-panel envelope (recommended) vs three independent per-panel fetches to the existing endpoints. Aggregate gives one round trip, one auth check, one `generatedAt`, one latency number; per-panel needs no composition code but still needs a new eligibility endpoint for quick actions.
- T2: dashboard-first as the user directed (recommended) vs a phase-0 experiment that redirects straight to "resume assigned work" behind the same flag, letting the metric decide whether the panels earn their place. The outside reviewer favored the experiment; the user's design doc names three distinct member needs the dashboard serves.
